claims.claim: Deletion of Prdm16 in adipocytes led to ablation of beige adipocyte function and dramatically reduced parenchymal innervation density.
claims.source: Specifically, deletion of Prdm16 in adipocytes led to ablation of beige adipocyte function and dramatically reduced parenchymal innervation density, suggesting that beige adipocyte-associated factors regulate the structure of sympathetic innervation.
claims.evidence: This is cited from the authors' previous work (Chi et al., 2018b).

claims.claim: At P2, adipocytes in iWAT appeared fully vascularized and organized into distinct lobular structures.
claims.source: At this stage, adipocytes appeared fully vascularized and organized into distinct lobular structures, as shown by the endothelial cell marker PECAM (also known as CD31) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,C and F), consistent with previous reports (Hong et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,C and F) and cited from Hong et al., 2015.

claims.claim: Dense parenchymal innervation in close apposition to adipocytes was not obvious at P2.
claims.source: While we could detect TH-positive (TH+) signals resembling nerve fascicles as well as fibers wrapping around large blood vessels, dense parenchymal innervation in close apposition to adipocytes, which was reported in adult iWAT (Chi et al., 2018b; Jiang et al., 2017), was not obvious at this age (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–F).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–F).

claims.claim: At P6, sympathetic fibers in iWAT travel in parallel within nerve fascicles.
claims.source: At P6, more distinct features of sympathetic innervation in iWAT were observed: (a) travelling in parallel within nerve fascicles and (b) wrapping around main blood vessels in a dense mesh-like morphology (Figure 1A–C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–D).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 1A–C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–D).

claims.claim: At P6, sympathetic fibers in iWAT wrap around main blood vessels in a dense mesh-like morphology.
claims.source: At P6, more distinct features of sympathetic innervation in iWAT were observed: (a) travelling in parallel within nerve fascicles and (b) wrapping around main blood vessels in a dense mesh-like morphology (Figure 1A–C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–D).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 1A–C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–D).

claims.claim: Sympathetic fibers leave the nerve fascicle and wrap around the main blood vessel as the first order of innervation.
claims.source: Specifically, we found several convergence points where TH+ nerve fibers within a nerve fascicle deviated from the bundle and merged with the innervation of the central blood vessel (Figure 1B–C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and C, Figure 1—video 1), suggesting that sympathetic fibers leave the nerve fascicle and wrap around the main blood vessel as the first order of innervation.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from imaging data (Figure 1B–C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and C, Figure 1—video 1).

claims.claim: The main blood vessel innervation extends around branching arterioles and venules as the second order of innervation.
claims.source: Subsequently, the main blood vessel innervation extended around branching arterioles and venules as the second order of innervation (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 2E–F, Figure 1—video 1).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 2E–F, Figure 1—video 1).

claims.claim: The majority of nerve fibers follow capillaries to arrive in the tissue parenchyma.
claims.source: Lastly, discrete nerve fibers became apparent at the terminals of the second-order innervation to project into tissue parenchyma, where adipocytes are located. Notably, the majority of these nerve fibers appeared to follow capillaries to arrive in the tissue parenchyma (Figure 1E–F, Figure 1—figure supplement 2G–J).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 1E–F, Figure 1—figure supplement 2G–J).

claims.claim: Sympathetic axons in iWAT first grow along the vasculature before reaching the tissue parenchyma.
claims.source: The results from P2 and P6 samples indicate that the sympathetic axons in iWAT first grow along the vasculature before reaching the tissue parenchyma, consistent with previous findings showing that developing sympathetic axons follow the vasculature to reach their target organs (Glebova and Ginty, 2005).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the imaging data and cited from Glebova and Ginty, 2005.

claims.claim: Dense parenchymal innervation surrounding adipocytes is not established at P6.
claims.source: However, dense parenchymal innervation surrounding adipocytes, which several studies have characterized in mature iWAT (Chi et al., 2018b; Jiang et al., 2017), is not established at P6.
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data and cited from Chi et al., 2018b; Jiang et al., 2017.

claims.claim: Dense parenchymal neurites surrounding adipocytes first became apparent at P10 in the inguinal region.
claims.source: Remarkably, adipocyte-innervating neurites became apparent four days later. In the inguinal region, dense parenchymal neurites surrounding adipocytes were first found at P10, in particular within lobules at the core of this region (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 2K, Figure 1—figure supplement 3D, Figure 1—video 2).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 2K, Figure 1—figure supplement 3D, Figure 1—video 2).

claims.claim: At P14, the number of lobules containing dense parenchymal neurites dramatically increased in the inguinal region.
claims.source: At P14, the number of lobules that contain dense parenchymal neurites dramatically increased, spreading outwards from the core of the inguinal region (Figure 1H, Figure 1—figure supplement 3F, Figure 1—video 2).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 1H, Figure 1—figure supplement 3F, Figure 1—video 2).

claims.claim: The emergence of dense parenchymal neurites in the dorsomedial region lagged behind the inguinal region.
claims.source: Interestingly, the emergence of dense parenchymal neurites in the dorsomedial region lagged behind. While parenchymal neurites were detectable in the dorsomedial region at P14 and P21 (Figure 1H–I, Figure 1—figure supplement 2K–L, Figure 1—figure supplement 3E & G, Figure 1—video 2), we did not observe densely innervated lobules that resemble the adult innervation pattern in this region until P28 (Figure 1J, Figure 1—figure supplement 3I, Figure 1—video 2).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 1H–J, Figure 1—figure supplement 2K–L, Figure 1—figure supplement 3E,G,I, Figure 1—video 2).

claims.claim: The dorsolateral region of iWAT remained sparsely innervated relative to other regions throughout the early postnatal period.
claims.source: Notably, the dorsolateral region of iWAT remained sparsely innervated relative to the inguinal region and the dorsomedial region throughout the early postnatal period (Figure 1G–J, Figure 1—figure supplement 2K–L, Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,C,E,G & I, Figure 1—video 2).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 1G–J, Figure 1—figure supplement 2K–L, Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,C,E,G,I, Figure 1—video 2).

claims.claim: Beige adipocytes first emerge in iWAT at P6 in the core of the inguinal region.
claims.source: Specifically, we found that beige adipocytes first emerge in iWAT of P6 animals that were born and housed at room temperature, as shown by a few UCP1+ adipocytes sparsely distributed in the core of the inguinal region, close to the inguinal lymph node (Figure 2A–B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 2A–B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).

claims.claim: At P10, clusters of UCP1+ adipocytes were located in distinct lobules in the core of the inguinal region.
claims.source: At P10, we detected clusters of UCP1+ adipocytes located in distinct lobules in the core of the inguinal region (Figure 2C–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 2C–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).

claims.claim: At P14, lobules containing UCP1+ adipocytes expanded from the core of the inguinal region.
claims.source: Four days later, at P14, the lobules containing UCP1+ adipocytes further expanded from the core (Figure 2E & G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 2E,G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).

claims.claim: At P21 and P28, extensive UCP1+ lobules occupied a significant portion of the inguinal region.
claims.source: At P21 and P28, extensive UCP1+ lobules occupied a significant portion of the inguinal region, comparable to the extent of UCP1+ cells only seen in adult animals after cold exposure (Figure 2H and J, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,C,G, & H).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 2H,J, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,C,G,H).

claims.claim: UCP1+ adipocytes in the dorsomedial region first emerged in small clusters at P14.
claims.source: On the other hand, the emergence of UCP1+ adipocytes in the dorsolumbar region again lagged behind. UCP1+ adipocytes in the dorsomedial region first emerged in small clusters at P14 and then as distinct lobules at P21 (Figure 2E–F & and H–I).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 2E–F,H–I).

claims.claim: The dorsolateral region was devoid of UCP1+ adipocytes at all stages analyzed during early postnatal development.
claims.source: Interestingly, the dorsolateral region was devoid of UCP1+ adipocytes at all stages analyzed (Figure 2A,C,E and H, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A & D–H).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 2A,C,E,H, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,D–H).

claims.claim: Ucp1 mRNA expression showed a gradual increase from P6 to P14 in the inguinal region.
claims.source: In line with the imaging results, Ucp1 mRNA expression showed a gradual increase from P6 to P14 in the inguinal region (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: This is based on qPCR data (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).

claims.claim: Ucp1 mRNA levels peaked around P12-P16 in the inguinal region.
claims.source: To our surprise, although we observed more extensive UCP1+ adipocytes in the inguinal region at P21 and P28 by imaging, Ucp1 mRNA levels peaked around P12-P16, with the expression level at P14 being fourfold and eightfold higher than that of P21 and P28, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: This is based on qPCR data (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).

claims.claim: Beige adipocytes arising in the inguinal region during early postnatal development may exhibit peak thermogenic potential around 2–3 weeks of age.
claims.source: These quantitative transcriptional data suggest that the beige adipocytes arising in the inguinal region of iWAT during early postnatal development may exhibit peak thermogenic potential around 2–3 weeks of age and gradually become less active as animals mature.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the qPCR data showing peak Ucp1 expression at P14.

claims.claim: Prdm16 showed a consistent 1.5- to twofold increase in mRNA levels in the inguinal relative to the dorsolumbar region across all time points.
claims.source: Of note, Prdm16, the transcriptional coregulator that determines beige adipocyte phenotype, showed a consistent 1.5- to twofold increase in mRNA levels in the inguinal relative to the dorsolumbar region across all time points (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
claims.evidence: This is based on qPCR data (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).

claims.claim: There is a dramatic overlap between the presence of dense parenchymal innervation and beige adipocytes from P10 onwards.
claims.source: When we overlaid the UCP1 and TH signals, we observed a dramatic overlap between the presence of dense parenchymal innervation and beige adipocytes, particularly from P10 onwards (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–J, Figure 1—video 2), strongly suggesting that early postnatal beige adipocytes are associated with the signals enabling sympathetic axon growth.
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–J, Figure 1—video 2).

claims.claim: Early postnatal beige adipocytes and sympathetic neurites arise in iWAT with the same patterning when mice are raised at 30°C as at room temperature.
claims.source: When mice were born and raised at a warmer temperature (30°C), at which cold-induced sympathetic firing is minimized, early postnatal beige adipocytes and sympathetic neurites arise in iWAT with the same patterning as that of room temperature-housed mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 3K–L).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 2—figure supplement 3K–L).

claims.claim: The development of beige adipocytes is likely not dependent on sympathetic activation.
claims.source: In addition, a recent study using genetic sympathetic ablation showed that early postnatal beige adipocytes develop normally in the absence of sympathetic innervation (Wu et al., 2020b). Together, these data suggest that the development of beige adipocytes is likely not dependent on sympathetic activation, but rather based on a developmentally hard-wired program.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the thermoneutrality data and cited from Wu et al., 2020b.

claims.claim: At P6, the sympathetic nervous system develops similarly in both control and cPrdm16KO mice.
claims.source: At P6, we observed minimal beige adipocytes and scant parenchymal innervation in both control and cPrdm16KO mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–H), suggesting that the sympathetic nervous system develops similarly in both models prior to the emergence of beige adipocyte clusters.
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–H).

claims.claim: At P14, deletion of Prdm16 completely ablated beige adipocytes in the inguinal region at both mRNA and protein levels.
claims.source: At P14, the deletion of Prdm16 completely ablated beige adipocytes that normally arise in the inguinal region of control mice, both at the mRNA and protein levels (Figure 3I, Figure 3—figure supplement 1I, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D).
claims.evidence: This is based on qPCR and imaging data (Figure 3I, Figure 3—figure supplement 1I, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D).

claims.claim: At P14, the increase in parenchymal innervation density in the inguinal region of control mice was not observed in cPrdm16KO mice.
claims.source: Correspondingly, the increase seen in parenchymal innervation density in the inguinal region of control mice was not observed in cPrdm16KO mice (Figure 3A–D, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 3A–D, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D).

claims.claim: At P21, cPrdm16KO mice showed ablation of beige adipocytes and lack of growth in parenchymal innervation.
claims.source: At P21, we observed similar ablation of beige adipocytes and lack of growth in parenchymal innervation in cPrdm16KO relative to control samples (Figure 3E–I, Figure 3—figure supplement 1I, Figure 3—figure supplement 2E–H).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging and qPCR data (Figure 3E–I, Figure 3—figure supplement 1I, Figure 3—figure supplement 2E–H).

claims.claim: Sympathetic axon growth during early iWAT morphogenesis may be regulated by PRDM16-dependent signals.
claims.source: These results indicate that early postnatal beige adipocytes indeed depend on PRDM16, the well-characterized transcriptional determinant of brown and beige adipocytes. Importantly, these data strongly suggest that sympathetic axon growth during early iWAT morphogenesis may be regulated by PRDM16-dependent signals.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the cPrdm16KO data showing loss of both beige adipocytes and sympathetic innervation.

claims.claim: Prdm16 appears to be minimally expressed in white adipocytes in iWAT.
claims.source: Altogether, Prdm16 appears to be minimally expressed in white adipocytes in iWAT, and thus its deletion in white adipocytes is likely to contribute minimally to the changes in sympathetic innervation.
claims.evidence: This is based on qPCR and western blot data showing low Prdm16 expression in the dorsolateral region.

claims.claim: Deletion of Prdm16 in iBAT does not affect its development or thermogenic function in young adults.
claims.source: Interestingly, although PRDM16 also plays a critical role in brown adipocyte determination and function, deletion of Prdm16 in interscapular brown fat (iBAT) does not affect its development or thermogenic function in young adults (Cohen et al., 2014; Harms et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is cited from Cohen et al., 2014; Harms et al., 2014.

claims.claim: The role of PRDM16 in iBAT formation and function is compensated for by PRDM3.
claims.source: Previous studies have shown that the role of PRDM16 in iBAT formation and function is compensated for by PRDM3, a transcriptional regulator closely related to PRDM16 (Harms et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is cited from Harms et al., 2014.

claims.claim: Similarly extensive sympathetic parenchymal innervation was detected in iBAT of both control and cPrdm16KO mice.
claims.source: Consistent with these findings, we detected similarly extensive sympathetic parenchymal innervation in iBAT of both control and cPrdm16KO mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 2K–L).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 3—figure supplement 2K–L).

claims.claim: Perinatal doxycycline treatment led to a strong reduction in Prdm16 in adipose depots at the mRNA level (70% reduction in the inguinal region of iWAT, 65% reduction in iBAT).
claims.source: We first confirmed that perinatal doxycycline treatment led to a strong reduction in Prdm16 in adipose depots at the mRNA (70% reduction in the inguinal region of iWAT, 65% reduction in iBAT) and protein levels (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–B).
claims.evidence: This is based on qPCR and western blot data (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–B).

claims.claim: iPrdm16KO (perinatal, 5 weeks) and littermate control mice developed similarly with no difference in body mass.
claims.source: Both iPrdm16KO (perinatal, 5 weeks) and littermate control mice developed similarly, with no difference in body mass (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This is based on body weight measurements (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).

claims.claim: Control inguinal regions exhibited robust increases in thermogenic markers following 2 days of cold exposure (e.g. 35-fold induction in Ucp1).
claims.source: As expected, the control inguinal regions exhibited robust increases in the entire panel of thermogenic markers following 2 days of cold exposure (e.g. 35-fold induction in Ucp1) (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This is based on qPCR data (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).

claims.claim: Cold-induced increases in thermogenic markers were almost completely blocked following perinatal deletion of Prdm16.
claims.source: In contrast, the cold-induced increases were almost completely blocked following perinatal deletion of Prdm16 (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D), mirroring our previous findings in constitutive Prdm16KO mice (Cohen et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is based on qPCR data (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D) and cited from Cohen et al., 2014.

claims.claim: Transient Prdm16 deletion did not significantly alter adipocyte differentiation or function, as shown by Pparg, Fabp4, and Adipoq mRNA levels.
claims.source: On the other hand, the transient Prdm16 deletion did not significantly alter adipocyte differentiation or function, as shown by Pparg, Fabp4, and Adipoq mRNA levels (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: This is based on qPCR data (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).

claims.claim: Gross features of sympathetic innervation such as nerve fascicles and blood vessel innervation were preserved in perinatal iPrdm16KO.
claims.source: While the gross features of sympathetic innervation such as nerve fascicles and blood vessel innervation were preserved in perinatal iPrdm16KO, the parenchymal innervation that localized to the inguinal region of control iWAT was dramatically reduced in perinatal iPrdm16KO (Figure 4D–I, Figure 4—video 1).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 4D–I, Figure 4—video 1).

claims.claim: Parenchymal innervation in the inguinal region of control iWAT was dramatically reduced in perinatal iPrdm16KO.
claims.source: While the gross features of sympathetic innervation such as nerve fascicles and blood vessel innervation were preserved in perinatal iPrdm16KO, the parenchymal innervation that localized to the inguinal region of control iWAT was dramatically reduced in perinatal iPrdm16KO (Figure 4D–I, Figure 4—video 1).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 4D–I, Figure 4—video 1).

claims.claim: Perinatal iPrdm16KO samples showed a 74.5% reduction in parenchymal neurite density compared to control samples when normalized to volume.
claims.source: When neurite lengths were normalized to volumes of the isolated cuboids, perinatal iPrdm16KO samples showed a 74.5% reduction in parenchymal neurite density compared to control samples (Figure 4J, Figure 4—figure supplement 2F).
claims.evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of imaging data (Figure 4J, Figure 4—figure supplement 2F).

claims.claim: Perinatal iPrdm16KO showed a significant 52.8% decrease in neurite density when normalized by adipocyte density.
claims.source: To rule out this possibility, we also calculated neurite density by factoring in adipocyte density from each tissue volume, and still observed a significant 52.8% decrease in density following perinatal Prdm16 deletion (Figure 4K, Figure 4—figure supplement 2E–F).
claims.evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of imaging data (Figure 4K, Figure 4—figure supplement 2E–F).

claims.claim: Perinatal Prdm16 knockout in adipocytes did not significantly affect thermogenic or adipogenic markers in iBAT.
claims.source: Similar to our previous findings with the cPrdm16KO model, perinatal Prdm16 knockout in adipocytes did not significantly affect thermogenic or adipogenic markers in iBAT (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A–B).
claims.evidence: This is based on qPCR data (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A–B).

claims.claim: Sympathetic parenchymal innervation levels did not appear different between control and perinatal iPrdm16KO iBAT samples.
claims.source: In line with this, the sympathetic parenchymal innervation levels did not appear different between control and perinatal iPrdm16KO iBAT samples (Figure 4—figure supplement 3C–D).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 4—figure supplement 3C–D).

claims.claim: TH+ fibers appeared substantially sparser in iPrdm16KO (perinatal, 8 weeks) than control.
claims.source: Importantly, TH+ fibers still appeared substantially sparser in iPrdm16KO (perinatal, 8 weeks) than control (Figure 4—figure supplement 4E–J).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 4—figure supplement 4E–J).

claims.claim: Interactions between beige adipocytes and sympathetic nerve endings during an early critical developmental window are required for establishment of the sympathetic network in iWAT.
claims.source: Taken together, these results demonstrate that interactions between beige adipocytes and sympathetic nerve endings during an early critical developmental window are required for establishment of the sympathetic network in iWAT, as perturbations during this window lead to lasting effects on parenchymal innervation density.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the perinatal Prdm16 deletion experiments showing lasting effects on innervation.

claims.claim: Doxycycline treatment in adult mice led to a robust reduction in Prdm16 at the mRNA level (83% in the inguinal region of iWAT at RT).
claims.source: As expected, doxycycline treatment in adult mice led to a robust reduction in Prdm16 at the mRNA (83% in the inguinal region of iWAT at RT) and protein levels (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is based on qPCR and western blot data (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).

claims.claim: No body mass difference was observed between iPrdm16KO (adult deletion) and control mice.
claims.source: No body mass difference was observed between iPrdm16KO (adult deletion) and control mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is based on body weight measurements (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).

claims.claim: Significant attenuation of cold-induced upregulation in all thermogenic markers was observed following adult Prdm16 deletion.
claims.source: We also observed significant attenuation of cold-induced upregulation in all thermogenic markers following Prdm16 deletion (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This is based on qPCR data (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).

claims.claim: Adult Prdm16 deletion did not significantly alter markers of adipocyte differentiation.
claims.source: Consistent with our previous findings, Prdm16 deletion did not significantly alter markers of adipocyte differentiation (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This is based on qPCR data (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).

claims.claim: Dense sympathetic parenchymal innervation was present in the inguinal regions of iWAT from both iPrdm16KO (adult deletion) and control samples.
claims.source: Interestingly, we found dense sympathetic parenchymal innervation present in the inguinal regions of iWAT from both iPrdm16KO (adult deletion) and control samples (Figure 5C–H, Figure 4—video 1).
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging data (Figure 5C–H, Figure 4—video 1).

claims.claim: Quantitative analysis resulted in a small, insignificant decrease (17.6%) in neurite density in adult iPrdm16KO relative to control samples when normalized by volume.
claims.source: Quantitative analysis of the parenchymal neurite density (normalized by volume) from the 3D images resulted in a small, insignificant decrease (17.6%) in neurite density in adult iPrdm16KO relative to control samples (Figure 5I).
claims.evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of imaging data (Figure 5I).

claims.claim: Neurite density in adult iPrdm16KO was slightly higher (1.23-fold) than that of controls when normalized by adipocyte density.
claims.source: Furthermore, as the adipocytes appeared larger in adult iPrdm16KO samples (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E–J), we normalized neurite length by adipocyte density. As a result, we observed a reverse relationship with the neurite density in adult iPrdm16KO being slightly higher (1.23-fold) than that of controls (Figure 5J).
claims.evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of imaging data (Figure 5J).

claims.claim: Deleting Prdm16 in adipocytes of adult animals causes minimal changes in sympathetic parenchymal neurite density.
claims.source: These results suggest that the small density difference when normalized by volume is likely driven by a scaling effect rather than actual neurite remodeling. Importantly, these data indicate that deleting Prdm16 in adipocytes of adult animals causes minimal changes in sympathetic parenchymal neurite density, strongly supporting the early postnatal period being the critical window during which interactions between beige adipocytes and sympathetic nerve endings occur.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the quantitative analysis showing no significant change in innervation after adult Prdm16 deletion.

claims.claim: Dense sympathetic parenchymal innervation is observed in both iBAT and the inguinal region of iWAT where beige adipocytes are primarily located.
claims.source: Dense sympathetic parenchymal innervation is observed in both iBAT and the inguinal region of iWAT, where beige adipocytes are primarily located; however, sparse innervation is found in eWAT and the dorsolateral region of iWAT, an area of the tissue that is devoid of beige adipocytes even under long term cold stimulation (Chi et al., 2018b; Dichamp et al., 2019; Huesing et al., 2020; Murano et al., 2009; Zeng et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is cited from multiple studies (Chi et al., 2018b; Dichamp et al., 2019; Huesing et al., 2020; Murano et al., 2009; Zeng et al., 2019).

claims.claim: Sparse innervation is found in eWAT and the dorsolateral region of iWAT, areas devoid of beige adipocytes even under long term cold stimulation.
claims.source: Dense sympathetic parenchymal innervation is observed in both iBAT and the inguinal region of iWAT, where beige adipocytes are primarily located; however, sparse innervation is found in eWAT and the dorsolateral region of iWAT, an area of the tissue that is devoid of beige adipocytes even under long term cold stimulation (Chi et al., 2018b; Dichamp et al., 2019; Huesing et al., 2020; Murano et al., 2009; Zeng et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is cited from multiple studies (Chi et al., 2018b; Dichamp et al., 2019; Huesing et al., 2020; Murano et al., 2009; Zeng et al., 2019).

claims.claim: The appearance of UCP1+ beige adipocytes precedes the emergence of dense parenchymal neurites during early postnatal development.
claims.source: Importantly, the appearance of UCP1+ beige adipocytes precedes the emergence of dense parenchymal neurites during early postnatal development.
claims.evidence: This is based on the temporal analysis of UCP1+ adipocytes and TH+ neurites in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Sympathetic fibers travel in nerve fascicles to arrive at iWAT, and then depart from nerve fascicles to reach main blood vessels within iWAT.
claims.source: We observed that sympathetic fibers travel in nerve fascicles to arrive at iWAT, and then depart from nerve fascicles to reach main blood vessels within iWAT.
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging observations described in the Results section.

claims.claim: By P6, the sympathetic innervation on blood vessels demonstrated a dense mesh-like structure, resembling that of mature iWAT.
claims.source: By P6, the sympathetic innervation on blood vessels demonstrated a dense mesh-like structure, resembling that of mature iWAT.
claims.evidence: This is based on imaging observations described in the Results section.

claims.claim: Vasculature serves as a guide to direct developing sympathetic fibers to reach their targets.
claims.source: However, dense parenchymal innervation surrounding adipocytes, which several studies have characterized in mature iWAT (Chi et al., 2018b; Jiang et al., 2017), is not established at P6. Instead, we observed sparse discrete sympathetic fibers and small vessels in congruence within the tissue parenchyma, a common phenomenon in sympathetic nerve fiber development where vasculature serves as a guide to direct developing fibers to reach their targets, such as the heart (Nam et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is cited from Nam et al., 2013.

claims.claim: Early postnatal beige adipocytes develop normally in mice born and raised at thermoneutrality with minimal sympathetic activity.
claims.source: Although beige adipocyte recruitment in adult mice requires sympathetic stimulation, early postnatal beige adipocytes develop normally in mice born and raised at thermoneutrality with minimal sympathetic activity as well as in mice with genetic sympathetic ablation (Wu et al., 2020b).
claims.evidence: This is based on the thermoneutrality data in the manuscript and cited from Wu et al., 2020b.

claims.claim: Early postnatal beige adipocytes develop normally in mice with genetic sympathetic ablation.
claims.source: Although beige adipocyte recruitment in adult mice requires sympathetic stimulation, early postnatal beige adipocytes develop normally in mice born and raised at thermoneutrality with minimal sympathetic activity as well as in mice with genetic sympathetic ablation (Wu et al., 2020b).
claims.evidence: This is cited from Wu et al., 2020b.

claims.claim: Adipocytes or their progenitors in different regions of iWAT may exhibit unique properties.
claims.source: Interestingly, we found several genes involved in the transcriptional control of beige adipocyte determination and function to have higher expression levels in the inguinal than the dorsolumbar region throughout early development, suggesting adipocytes or their progenitors in different regions may exhibit unique properties.

results.result: Sympathetic innervation of iWAT develops in a stereotyped pattern during early postnatal life (P2-P28). Nerve fibers first travel along blood vessels (P2-P6), then dense parenchymal innervation surrounding adipocytes emerges between P10-P28, with regional differences in timing (inguinal region before dorsomedial, dorsolateral remains sparse).
results.evaluation: The developmental timeline is well-documented through systematic whole-tissue imaging at multiple time points (C31-C43) with clear morphological descriptions and regional analysis. The hierarchical pattern of innervation (nerve fascicles → blood vessels → parenchyma) is supported by detailed imaging evidence (C33-C37, C90-C91). The temporal progression and regional differences are consistently demonstrated across multiple animals.

results.result: UCP1+ beige adipocytes emerge in iWAT during early postnatal development (P6-P28) with a spatiotemporal pattern similar to sympathetic innervation. Beige adipocytes first appear at P6 in the inguinal region core, expand through P28, with peak thermogenic gene expression at P12-P16 that subsequently declines despite continued spatial expansion.
results.evaluation: The emergence and distribution of beige adipocytes is well-documented through UCP1 immunostaining at multiple time points (C44-C49) and corroborated by qPCR analysis (C50-C51). The discrepancy between increasing UCP1+ cell numbers and declining Ucp1 mRNA levels (C51-C52) is appropriately noted and interpreted as reduced thermogenic activity per cell. Regional expression differences in Prdm16 and other beige markers (C53) support the spatial patterning observations.

results.result: Early postnatal beige adipocytes and dense sympathetic innervation show dramatic spatial and temporal overlap from P10 onwards. This developmental program occurs independently of sympathetic activation, as it proceeds normally at thermoneutrality (30°C) and in mice with genetic sympathetic ablation.
results.evaluation: The spatial overlap is demonstrated through dual-channel imaging (C54), and independence from sympathetic activity is shown through thermoneutrality experiments (C55) and supported by cited genetic ablation studies (C56, C93-C94). However, the thermoneutrality experiment appears to be a single observation without quantification or statistical analysis, which is a minor limitation. The conclusion about developmental programming (C95) is appropriately qualified as inference.

results.result: Constitutive adipocyte-specific deletion of Prdm16 (cPrdm16KO) eliminates early postnatal beige adipocytes and prevents the normal increase in sympathetic parenchymal innervation density in iWAT during development (P14-P21). This effect is specific to beige adipocyte-containing regions, as Prdm16 expression is minimal in white adipocytes and iBAT innervation is preserved.
results.evaluation: The constitutive knockout phenotype is well-characterized through imaging (C57-C60) and molecular analysis (C58) at multiple time points. The specificity to beige regions is supported by regional Prdm16 expression analysis (C62) and preserved iBAT innervation (C65). The inference that PRDM16-dependent signals regulate sympathetic growth (C61) is reasonable but remains mechanistic speculation. Sample sizes appear adequate (n=2-3 for molecular, ≥3 for imaging) though statistical details are limited for some comparisons.

results.result: Inducible deletion of Prdm16 during the perinatal period (E14-P21) causes lasting reduction in sympathetic parenchymal innervation density (52.8-74.5% decrease) that persists to at least 8 weeks of age, while gross innervation features and adipocyte differentiation markers remain normal. This demonstrates a critical developmental window for beige adipocyte-mediated establishment of sympathetic structure.
results.evaluation: The perinatal deletion experiments are well-controlled with appropriate littermate controls, confirmed knockout efficiency (C66), and preserved general adipocyte function (C70). The innervation phenotype is rigorously quantified using 3D imaging with both volume-normalized and adipocyte-density-normalized metrics (C73-C74), addressing potential confounding by cell size changes. The persistence of the phenotype to 8 weeks (C77) supports the critical window interpretation (C78). Sample sizes (n=3 biological replicates with 4-8 technical replicates each) and statistical analysis appear adequate.

results.result: Deletion of Prdm16 in adult mice (8 weeks old) does not significantly affect sympathetic parenchymal innervation density in iWAT, despite reducing thermogenic gene expression. This demonstrates that Prdm16-dependent signals from beige adipocytes are not required for maintaining established sympathetic structure in mature animals.
results.evaluation: The adult deletion experiments provide strong evidence for the developmental window hypothesis through appropriate timing (8 weeks), confirmed knockout (C79), and preserved innervation despite functional changes (C81, C83-C85). The quantitative analysis accounts for adipocyte size differences (C85) and shows no significant change or even slight increase when normalized appropriately. The interpretation that the small volume-normalized decrease (17.6%, non-significant) is due to scaling rather than remodeling (C86) is well-reasoned. This result effectively contrasts with the perinatal deletion, strengthening the critical window conclusion.

results.result: Beige adipocyte-sympathetic neurite communication is crucial for establishing sympathetic structure during early postnatal development but dispensable for maintenance in mature animals. Sympathetic neurite density is regulated by local cues from beige adipocytes during a specific developmental window and exhibits limited plasticity once established.
results.evaluation: These main conclusions (C8-C9, C105) are well-supported by the combined evidence from developmental timing studies, constitutive knockout, perinatal deletion, and adult deletion experiments. The inference about limited plasticity (C105) is appropriately qualified and supported by the contrast between perinatal and adult deletion effects. However, the specific molecular mechanisms remain unidentified (acknowledged in C98-C101), and the conclusion about 'communication' is somewhat stronger than warranted since direct signaling has not been demonstrated—only spatial/temporal correlation and genetic dependence.

results.result: S100b shows regional and PRDM16-dependent expression patterns during early iWAT development, suggesting it may be one potential molecular cue regulating sympathetic development, though other beige adipocyte-associated cell types may also contribute indirectly.
results.evaluation: While S100b expression patterns are documented (C99), the functional role remains speculative (C98, C100). The claim is appropriately presented as hypothesis-generating rather than conclusive. No functional experiments (e.g., S100b deletion or blocking) are performed to test causality. The suggestion of indirect regulation through other cell types (C101) is pure speculation without supporting data. This represents preliminary correlative evidence requiring substantial follow-up work.

results.result: Prior work has established that beige adipocytes associate with dense sympathetic innervation in iWAT, that this density depends on PRDM16, and that thermogenic adipocyte-containing depots show dense innervation while white adipocyte depots show sparse innervation.
results.evaluation: These claims accurately represent established findings from prior literature (C1, C23, C87-C88) and the authors' previous work (C28-C30). The citations appear appropriate and the characterizations are consistent with the cited studies. This background appropriately motivates the current developmental study.

results.result: Prior studies have shown that Prdm16 deletion does not affect iBAT in young adults due to PRDM3 compensation, and that leptin-mediated central regulation can rescue sympathetic innervation defects in leptin-deficient mice, with the leptin surge timing overlapping the observed sympathetic growth period.
results.evaluation: These claims accurately cite relevant prior work (C63-C64, C106) and note an interesting temporal correlation with the postnatal leptin surge (C107). The citations appear accurate and the discussion appropriately contextualizes the current findings within the broader literature on adipose innervation regulation. However, no experiments are performed to test the relationship between leptin and the observed developmental program.

results.result: Background on adipose tissue biology, obesity epidemiology, thermogenic adipocyte function, and sympathetic regulation establishes the physiological and clinical context for studying beige adipocyte-sympathetic interactions.
results.evaluation: These introductory claims accurately represent established knowledge in the field with appropriate citations. They provide necessary context but do not constitute novel findings from this study. The characterizations of adipose tissue function (C10-C11, C17), obesity statistics (C14-C16), thermogenic adipocyte properties (C18-C22), and sympathetic regulation (C24-C27, C92) are well-established and appropriately cited.
